Subject: Interim: benchmark snapshot (FP16/BF16 vs INT8/INT4)

Elaine / team —

Quick interim update with a snapshot of synthetic and replay-based runs we completed on your eval set (attached: kernel_profile_summary.pdf, benchmark_results_20270219.csv, ttft_plots_20270219.png). These are raw numbers from our staging cluster (H100 profile) — we'll run A100 next week for comparison. Key observations:

Summary numbers (avg payload 512 tokens):
- FP16/BF16 (baseline) @ 32 concurrency:
  - p50 latency: 88 ms
  - p95 latency: 175 ms
  - throughput: ~1450 tokens/sec (aggregate across GPU pool)
  - TTFT warm: 45 ms; TTFT cold container: 62 ms

- INT8 @ 32 concurrency:
  - p50 latency: 72 ms
  - p95 latency: 160 ms
  - throughput: ~1850 tokens/sec
  - TTFT warm: 47 ms; TTFT cold: 68 ms

- INT4 @ 32 concurrency (experimental):
  - p50 latency: 65 ms
  - p95 latency: 210 ms (tail regression observed)
  - throughput: ~2200 tokens/sec
  - TTFT warm: 55 ms; TTFT cold: 95 ms

Concurrency scaling notes (p95 latency):
- 1 -> 8 concurrency: near-linear improvement in token throughput; p95 remains well under 150ms for FP16/INT8.
- 32 -> 64: FP16 p95 increases to ~240 ms (memory/KV pressure); INT8 p95 ~220 ms.
- 120 concurrency: both FP16 and INT8 show elevated p95 (FP16 ~490 ms, INT8 ~420 ms) without batching/queueing adjustments; throughput sustained but with higher tails.

Kernel profile observations (see PDF):
- INT8 shows hot-path improvements in MatMul kernels and reduced memory bandwidth.
- INT4 introduced two slow paths for long-sequence rotary/attention where our current INT4 kernels fall back to higher-precision compute for stability; this explains the p95 tail and TTFT cold jump on INT4.
- On H100 the INT8 speedup is ~1.25x vs FP16 for the observed traces; INT4 best-case 1.5x but inconsistent at long seq.

Regression checks:
- We ran 2500 eval prompts; INT8 avg embedding-similarity drop vs FP16: 0.7% (within gate); INT4 avg drop: 3.9% with ~5% of prompts flagged as degraded (we flagged examples).
- We recommend INT8 as the default quant path for production; INT4 only in read-heavy low-latency contexts after further kernel work.

Action items we propose:
- Short-run: enable INT8 in staging canary and collect 48-hour production parity metrics (latency, error-rate, quality sampling).
- Medium-run: iterate on INT4 kernel fallbacks (reduce fallback cases) and re-run regression suite.
- Procurement: we'll draft a recommended Dedicated capacity request showing required GPU counts for p95 SLOs at 120 concurrency (attached in the MAP).

Happy to walk through live — propose Tue 23 Feb 10:00 PT for a one-hour technical review + procurement sync.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
